title: Ethics Advisory Opinion No. 26-010-E
summary: A retired former state employee may work for a private business in relation to a contract with the state agency which was authorized after his retirement. Section 25-4-105(3)(e), Miss. Code of 1972, only prohibits a former public servant from working on the same matters in which he or she was directly or personally involved while working for the government.

ETHICS ADVISORY OPINION NO. 26-010-E
June 5, 2026
Question Presented: May a retired former state employee work for a private business in
relation to a contract with the state agency which was authorized
after his retirement?
Brief Answer: Yes. Section 25-4-105(3)(e), Miss. Code of 1972, only prohibits a
former public servant from working on the same matters in which
he or she was directly or personally involved while working for the
government.
The Mississippi Ethics Commission issued this opinion on the date shown above in
accordance with Section 25-4-17(i), Mississippi Code of 1972, as reflected upon its minutes of
even date. The Commission is empowered to interpret and opine only upon Article IV, Section
109, Mississippi Constitution of 1890, and Article 3, Chapter 4, Title 25, Mississippi Code of 1972.
This opinion does not interpret or offer protection from liability for any other laws, rules or
regulations. The Commission based this opinion solely on the facts and circumstances provided
by the requestor as restated herein. The protection from liability provided under Section 25-4-17(i)
is limited to the individual who requested this opinion and to the accuracy and completeness of
these facts.
I. LAW
The pertinent Ethics in Government Laws to be considered here are as follows:
Section 25-4-103, Miss. Code of 1972.
(c) “Business” means any corporation, partnership, sole proprietorship, firm,
enterprise, franchise, association, organization, holding company, self-employed
individual, joint stock company, receivership, trust or other legal entity or
undertaking organized for economic gain, a nonprofit corporation or other such
entity, association or organization receiving public funds.

(e) “Compensation” means money or thing of value received, or to be received,
from any person for services rendered.
(m) “Person” means any individual, firm, business, corporation, association,
partnership, union or other legal entity, and where appropriate a governmental
entity.
(p) “Public servant” means:
(i) Any elected or appointed official of the government;
(ii) Any officer, director, commissioner, supervisor, chief, head, agent or
employee of the government or any agency thereof, or of any public entity
created by or under the laws of the state of Mississippi or created by an
agency or governmental entity thereof, any of which is funded by public
funds or which expends, authorizes or recommends the use of public funds;
or
(iii) Any individual who receives a salary, per diem or expenses paid in
whole or in part out of funds authorized to be expended by the government.
Section 25-4-105, Miss. Code of 1972.
(3) No public servant shall:
(e) Perform any service for any compensation for any person or business
after termination of his office or employment in relation to any case,
decision, proceeding or application with respect to which he was directly
concerned or in which he personally participated during the period of his
service or employment.
II. FACTS
Facts provided by the requestor are set forth below, with identifying information redacted, and
are considered a part of this opinion.
I…do hereby respectfully submit this Request for an Opinion such that I may be
allowed to serve as the Senior Project Manager for the subject project. After
retiring from [a state agency] on February 15, 2022, I have been working with a
consulting firm…. Some of my duties in the following positions held during my
time at [the state agency] are included below for reference:
• …Division Director (2020-2021) – send recommendations to …
Administration for consultant selection on projects determined to have no available
in-house staff to complete the work. The decision of which consultant to select is
a collaborative effort that evaluates consultants based on factors such as current
workload (availability of staff), ability to perform the specific tasks of the project,

and past performance on similar projects. Final approval of the recommended
consultant is made by the [agency] Administration, including the [top executives].
• Assistant … Division Director (2015 – 2020) – worked as the Assistant
Project Manager for all … Division projects in the state. This role included
supervising individual Assistant Project Managers and determining when to assign
projects to in-house staff versus hiring consultants. Once a decision was made to
hire a consultant for a project, a consultant was selected as described above.
• Assistant Project Manager (2002 – 2015) – ensure that all projects were
designed according to … Division standards and completed within the allotted
schedule for a district within the state. Initiate selection forms for projects to be
assigned to consultants as directed by my supervisor and forward to the Division
Director for approval.
The reason for the Request for Opinion on the subject project is as follows:
Due to the lack of available in-house staff to complete the work, [my employer]
was selected by [the state agency] from the 2014 … Master contract in October
2016 to complete Phase A Final … Plans and Phase B Final … Plans for the subject
project. Numerous scope-of-work changes occurred which resulted in additional
contracts as stated below:
• New contract in January 2018 with the same deliverable requirements as the
original contract but with modified project limits and scope of work changes.
• Supplemental agreement in October 2023 to remove Phase B Final … Plans
from the January 2018 contract.
• Supplemental agreement in November 2023 to remove Phase B Final … Plans
from the October 2016 work assignment and therefore terminated this contract.
The Phase A Final … plans were completed in November 2025, and the January
2018 contract was terminated in December 2025. In January 2026, [the state
agency] selected [my current employer] to complete the Phase B Final … plans
under a new work assignment from the 2023 … Master contract.
As … Division Director, I inherited the role of Project Manager of all ongoing
consultant projects, including the subject project. I was neither a member of the
selection committee for the 2014 or 2017 … Master contracts used to execute nor
a participant in selecting [my current employer] for the work assignments listed
above. My only involvement with this project was as follows:
• Invoice Signatures - After review and concurrence from the project
[professional], approved invoices as they were received.
• Project Assistance - As requested by the project [professional] assigned to
oversee the day-to-day management of the project, assisted with general …
questions.

In summary, I had no management duties of or any other related responsibilities to
the subject project other than those described in the above bullet points. I
respectfully request that you issue an opinion that I may serve as [my current
employer’s] Senior Project Manager for this project.
III. ANALYSIS
Section 25-4-105(3)(e), Miss. Code of 1972, addresses successive government and private
sector employment. Section 25-4-105(3)(e) will not necessarily prohibit a former public servant
from being employed by an entity which contracts with his or her former government employer.
The law merely prohibits the former public servant from working for pay in the private sector on
any matter in which he or she was directly or personally involved while working for the
government.
Therefore, if the former public servant was not directly concerned with and did not
personally participate in the matter in question, then the former public servant may legally accept
payment from the private entity to work on that matter. Elec. Data Sys. Corp. v. Miss. Div. of
Medicaid, 853 So.2d 1192, 1204, 1205 (¶¶ 35, 39) (Miss. 2003). If the former public servant was
directly concerned with and did personally participate in the matter in question, then the private
entity may still contract with the government, but the former public servant may not be paid in
relation to that matter. Id.
The matter in question here is the contract to complete Phase B final plans. According to
the facts provided above, that contract began in January 2026, pursuant to a master contract
approved in 2023. The requestor retired from the state agency in 2022. Therefore, the requestor
had no direct or personal involvement as a state employee in the current contract and is not
prohibited from working for his current employer as senior project manager for this project.
